CLINICAL INDICATION:  ___ man with Crohn's flare.  Evaluate for

FINDINGS:

There is a paucity of gas seen within the abdomen, likely related to

Osseous structures show no abnormalities.  Lung bases are clear.

REASON FOR EXAMINATION:  Crohn disease with severe abdominal pain.

Supine and erect radiographs of the abdomen were obtained in AP projection and
compared to ___.

Compared to the prior study there is increase in the bowel loops diameter with
the current small bowel loops being up to 4 cm in diameter in particular in
the left upper quadrant with more of dilatation seen along the colon and
several nonspecific air-fluid levels demonstrated.  There is no clear evidence
of air within the rectosigmoid.  Although the findings are nonspecific they
might represent some partial small-bowel obstruction and if clinically
warranted should be further evaluated with cross-sectional imaging.  There is
no free air below the diaphragms.

HISTORY:  ___ male with history of Crohn's disease, now with acutely
worsening abdominal pain concerning for abscess or perforation.

COMPARISON:  CT abdomen/pelvis last performed on ___.

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT axial imaging is performed through the abdomen and pelvis
after administration of water-soluble oral contrast and 130 mL of IV Optiray
350.  Multiplanar reformatted images were then obtained.

CT ABDOMEN WITH IV CONTRAST:  Mild dependent atelectatic changes are noted in
the visualized lung bases.  No pleural or pericardial effusion is seen.

The liver, gallbladder, pancreas, adrenal glands and left kidney appear
unremarkable.  Small area of relative hypodensity along the falciform ligament
in the liver likely represents an area of focal fatty infiltration. The spleen
has increased in size since ___, currently measuring 14.1-cm on sagittal
imaging and previously measuring 12.4-cm on ___ and 10.0 cm on ___. A
tiny 5- mm hypodensity in the lower pole of the right kidney is too small to
accurately characterize but likely represents a tiny cyst and is unchanged.

Oral contrast is seen to the level of the rectum.  The stomach and small bowel
appear normal in the abdomen.  The patient is status post subtotal colectomy,
with ileosigmoid anastomosis.  Again, there is circumferential wall
thickening, slight irregularity, mild fat stranding and somewhat tethered
appearance to region of the ileosigmoid anastomosis.  Allowing for comparison
between the current study where this loop is nearly collapsed and the prior
studies where this loop is well distended, the extent and severity of findings
is likely little changed.  No free fluid, abscess, extravasated contrast, or
free air is demonstrated.

The abdominal aorta maintains normal caliber throughout.  Mesenteric and
retroperitoneal nodes are subcentimeter, not meeting CT size criteria for
adenopathy.

CT PELVIS WITH IV CONTRAST:  The urinary bladder, distal ureters, prostate,
and seminal vesicles appear normal.  No pelvic free fluid, free air, or
adenopathy is noted.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:  A 7-mm sclerotic focus in the right iliac bone adjacent
to the sacroiliac joints has been present since ___ and is little changed
since then, likely representing a bone island.  Slight convex right curvature
of the spine may be positional.

IMPRESSIONS:
1.  Bowel wall thickening, mild fat stranding and slight tethered appearance
to the region of the ileosigmoid anastomosis appears little changed compared
to ___, allowing for differences in bowel distention.  No evidence of
bowel perforation, obstruction or abscess.
2.  Splenomegaly is increased from prior studies; clinical correlation
recommended.
